title: The Fall of Nineveh (612 BC)
lead: In 612 BC the Babylonians and the Medes took and burned Nineveh, ending the Assyrian empire in all but name. The main source is the Babylonian Chronicle ABC 3; Nahum and Zephaniah 2:13-15 are the biblical witnesses.

sections.b: The Babylonian Chronicle tells of a siege of about three months, the death of the Assyrian king and the carrying off of the city's spoil. The last Assyrian army held out at Harran until about 609 BC. Later Greek writers (Ctesias, through Diodorus Siculus) add a story of a flood of the Tigris; that is late and uncertain. The biblical books treat the fall as the LORD's judgment.
